server.mjs rebuild written and syntax-clean. Design note for the critic: THREE layers between bucket and caller, ordered so the load-bearing one needs no secret. (1) provenanceBlock() is the ONLY constructor of a provenance block, called on render and on hit alike, and `arrival:'placed'` is asserted not parameterised - no input makes it say anything else. (2) sha256(png) must equal the manifest's recorded hash. (3) HMAC over {cache_key,sha256,bytes,spec,settle,build_key,captured_at} keyed from CACHE_KEY_PATH (0600). Any failure = MISS, not error. The MAC's honest limit is written into the code: all agents run as the same user so it authenticates 'this daemon wrote this', not 'no hostile process could forge it'; layer 1 is what holds in that case.

CACHE-HIT VERIFICATION, first attempt INVALID and why it matters: two identical specs 61 s apart both rendered (cached:false, 61.0 s then 62.8 s). Not a defect - the daemon log shows 'BUILD CHANGED game@bd9b5ece0bd54658 -> game@350cb91ccc884b54' between them, so the second request landed in a different bucket and correctly missed. Notably readCache() logged NO rejection, which is the right signature for 'the entry was never there' as against 'the entry was there and refused'. Re-running against a --pin-build daemon, which freezes the build key at boot so another agent editing game/ cannot move the bucket mid-test. LESSON FOR ANY AGENT MEASURING CACHE BEHAVIOUR ON THIS BOX: without --pin-build, a two-request cache test is measuring other agents' edit rate, not the cache.
